content.text: {"per_criterion": {"heroes": "B", "craft": "B", "facts": "TIE", "age_fit": "TIE", "continuity": "B", "delight": "B"}, "verdict": "B", "confidence": 0.95, "justification": "These two stories are almost word for word the same, with the same plot, facts, sound words and warm goodnight ending. The difference is that Story A keeps using Cruz's name where Phoenix should be. Cruz suggests both company names back to back. \"Cruz grabbed Cruz's hand\" during the fire. \"Cruz carried planks. Cruz handed out nails.\" Kjeld invites only Cruz to build, and Cruz both starts and finishes the closing reflection. After the first chapter, Phoenix all but disappears from Story A, so one of the two heroes is lost. A parent reading it aloud would stumble over lines that make no sense, and a child listening for their own name would notice it missing. Story B shares the discoveries fairly: Phoenix names the Duck Company, spots the first plastic brick, tests the new clicking brick and carries the glowing brick home, while Cruz comes up with the tubes idea. Both children drive the story and both are shown in a good light. The facts, age fit and length are the same in both, so they tie there. Story B wins on heroes, craft, continuity and read-aloud delight."}
